uploads.title: What If Quantum Computers Broke All Encryption?
uploads.caption: What If Quantum Computers Broke All Encryption?
uploads.description:
Every card payment, private message and bank login is protected by math that would take today's supercomputers millions of years to crack. A big enough quantum computer could break it in days. Experts call that moment Q-Day. How public-key encryption works, why the number of qubits needed to break it keeps shrinking, what would happen on Q-Day, why millions of bitcoin (including Satoshi's) are exposed, and the race to switch the internet to post-quantum locks.

Sources: Caltech/Oratomic preprint (2026); Gidney (2025); Iceberg Quantum (2026); Google Quantum AI ECDLP whitepaper (2026); Quantum Alliance estimate (Oct 2026); NIST FIPS 203/204/205 (2024); NIST IR 8547 draft (2024).
Narration: AI voice (ElevenLabs).
